description.narrative: The IMVO Renewable Energy Agreement establishes agreements to comply with internationalstandards for responsible business conduct in the production chains of participating companies.Together, the parties will focus on preventing and mitigating the (potential) negative consequencesof the energy transition for people, nature, the environment, and biodiversity. This will be achievedby supportingand monitoring the activities and efforts of companies to improve their productionchains, thereby identifying risks and subsequently preventing, mitigating, or compensating for them.Furthermore, the collective leverage will be used to encourage companies to take actions thatpositively impact renewable energy production chains. This can be achieved, among other things,by taking the following steps:Incorporating the International RBC standards into the policies of companies and institutions, thusencouraging suppliers to source their products responsibly. To strive to reduce negative impacts onpeople, the environment, nature, and ecology, and to increasesocio-economic and ecologicalopportunities in the production chain (for example, by utilizing the best or new technologies androadmaps during the construction, operational phase, and decommissioning of offshore andonshore wind and solar farms).To guarantee labor rights – from the sourcing of materials to the construction and installation ofwind and solar farms. Workers should have the opportunity to join a union for bargaining, withoutrisk of unequal treatment or retaliation. The parties to the agreement therefore strive to implementinternational standards, such as the ILO Declaration on Fundamental Principles and Rights atWork, the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises, and the UN Guiding Principles forBusiness and Human Rights.To guarantee human rights throughout the entire value chain, including respecting the rights ofindigenous peoples and local communities, as presented in UNDRIP (such as the right of FreePrior and Informed Consent) and UNDROP.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
